messages:
alex_m: Alerting — sudden 12x spike in connections to /v1/embeddings from multiple VNFs in APAC and EU, origin ASN looks like 47808 and 24940. Backend queue depth increasing, some Dedicated nodes reporting 503s. Not normal traffic patterns.

maya_s: Ack. Pulling logs now. Any customer reports?

alex_m: No customer tickets yet, internal traces show lots of short-lived TCP connections with TLS1.3 SNI matching our generic hostnames. Patterns: high new-conn rate, low payload. Looks like connection-flood probing but with legitimate TLS handshake.

chris_r: Oncall — i'll open a mitigation window. Suggest: (1) enable conservative per-IP rate limit at edge (2) apply temporary WAF rule to challenge with JS challenge for non-browser UA (3) add ipset block for top abusive /24s.

lia_ops: I can push rate-limit change. Propose 200 rps per IP aggregate with burst 400 for embeddings route. Want to keep trusted partners exempt. Need RBAC to allow me to apply exemptions.

maya_s: We should avoid blanket blocks that hit paying customers. Can we create a short-lived RBAC change that grants lia_ops the 'mitigate:edge' role and logs all actions to audit? security_bot, is that approved?

security_bot: Temporary RBAC elevation OK under emergency policy, 2-hour TTL, must record reason and approver. All actions will be audited and shipped to KMS-encrypted log bucket. @lia_ops add ticket id and approver name in the audit message.

lia_ops: Doing that now. Creating role grant: CLI ->

```
redwood auth grant --user lia_ops --role mitigate:edge --ttl 2h --reason "DDoS mitigation 2039001111"
```
Will add ticket link.

sre-bot: Deploy bot: edge-rate-limit updated for /v1/embeddings: per-ip 200 rps, burst 400. WAF: add rule 90011 JS challenge for suspicious UA. ipset: add 203.0.113.0/24, 198.51.100.0/24.

alex_m: After rate limit and ipset push, connection rate dropped 70% from those subnets. Queue depth normalizing. Still seeing different ASN hitting fallback—looks like fast failover between pools.

chris_r: Good. Next: enable KV prefix caching for heavy prefix queries so legitimate users get fewer backend hits. Also schedule a canary to rollback rules in 15 minutes if error rate > 1%.

maya_s: About audit logs: confirm that mitigation actions (RBAC grant, WAF rule, ipset adds) are captured in our audit pipeline and encrypted with customer KMS key for retention. Who owns the KMS key policy?

sam_c: Security — KMS key for audits is managed by security-team-kms. We have an allow-list for principals; temporary mitigation role will be added to the allow-list for PutObject to the audit-bucket. I will add a policy statement now. Note: we will rotate the key alias after incident within 24h per policy.

security_bot: Policy change logged. Reminder: any KMS policy changes must be peer-reviewed. sam_c — ping @chris_r for review.

sam_c: Review requested. Pushing minimal policy to allow sts:AssumeRole from mitigate:edge for PutObject only.

emily-pm: Heads-up — we should prepare customer comms if any paid customers were impacted. Lia, do we have a quick impact list?

lia_ops: Running query for 24h requests with client_ip in blocked ranges -> mapping to account IDs. Preliminary: 3 accounts showed elevated errors for <5min each. All are low-traffic integrations.

chris_r: If impact minimal, we'll send an FYI post-incident. If any SLO breaches, escalate to sales/regulatory.

alex_m: One more finding: probe used rotating source IPs with short TTLs and randomized SNI. WAF JS challenge stopped most of the botland behavior but increased latency for some real mobile clients. We'll revert JS challenge to captcha 2-tier for mobile UA.

maya_s: Post-incident actions checklist: 1) Create detection rule for ASN rotation + low payload handshakes 2) Add automated ipset autoscaling for top N offending /24s 3) Harden RBAC playbook for mitigations 4) Validate audit pipeline end-to-end (KMS encryption + retention) 5) Write customer comms template and runbook.

lia_ops: I'm adding items to the incident ticket: INCIDENT-2039001111. Assigning owners: detections->alex_m, automations->chris_r, RBAC+audit->sam_c, comms->emily-pm.

sre-bot: Canary monitor active: rollback conditions not met. System stable for 18m.

chris_r: After stabilization we'll rotate any edge API keys that were exposed in logs and force short TTL for mitigation roles. Also schedule a tabletop next week to review KMS policy runbook.

sam_c: I'll prepare the KMS policy delta and a step-by-step for emergency grants, plus a checklist to ensure audit logs include role/grant metadata and reason string.

emily-pm: I'll draft the customer FYI and internal postmortem template. Let's aim for a 4-hour interim post and a 72-hour full postmortem.

alex_m: Thanks team. Marking incident as mitigated but still monitoring. Follow-ups captured in INCIDENT-2039001111. :thumbsup:
